response.markdown_report:
The next step should test whether GRU4Rec’s sampled training separation depends on candidate construction. At 10% progress, retain the bounded frequency-matched panel, with fresh sampling and an optional exact finite-pool reference. It cannot identify the cause of poor validation HR@10.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, all four categories pass reported execution checks; exported-predictor parity remains unmeasured. Behavioral diagnosis can proceed within that coverage. Second, Electronics has 14.49% sampled negative wins for low-frequency positives versus 2.86% for high-frequency positives. This motivates stratification, without establishing a held-out deficit or popularity bias. Third, temporal-effect estimates are omitted. Missing results cannot justify recency mechanisms or imply zero temporal dependence.

**Insights from related work.** First, Krichene and Rendle show that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons. Frequency matching is consequently a conditional stress test, not an unbiased correction. Second, Prakash et al. study training samplers using SASRec and full-catalog evaluation. Their frequency-cohort findings motivate stratification here, but do not validate matched evaluation negatives. Third, Hidasi and Karatzoglou demonstrate interactions between GRU4Rec losses and negative sampling. Their results support a subsequent controlled training experiment, without guaranteeing Amazon HR@10 gains.

These insights organize three directions: execution validity, candidate sensitivity, and training interventions. The framework separates controlled changes from supported conclusions:

| Direction | Controlled change | Supported interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Existing temporal panel | History order; fixed candidates | Conditional order sensitivity |
| Proposed candidate panel | Distractor distribution; fixed history/model | Conditional candidate sensitivity |
| Later training experiment | Sampler, then loss separately | Validation effect under fixed protocol |

Three diagnostic ideas and one training alternative follow. Scores are originality / future potential / code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency-matched candidate panel | 3 / 6 / 4 | Reproducible frequency control | Established ingredients; no causal explanation |
| Title-similar distractors | 4 / 6 / 4 | Tests textual associations | Similarity cannot label irrelevance |
| Hidden-state margin replay | 6 / 7 / 7 | Separates recurrence from scoring sensitivity | Requires architecture-specific instrumentation |
| Fixed-loss uniform versus frequency^0.5 training | 2 / 7 / 4 | Direct GRU4Rec precedent; tests predictive benefit | Retraining cost; loss-dependent effects |

**Selected idea: frequency-matched candidate panel.** Freeze explicitly indexed training-prefix histories, targets and checkpoints. Compare five fresh uniform candidate sets with five fresh sets matched to target-frequency bands, each containing 99 unique unseen negatives. Keep earlier frozen sets as separate realized results. Average draws within users before category summaries; report margins, strict negative-win fractions, ties and exclusions. Rank/HR requires the pinned ranking adapter.

When affordable, chunk-score complete eligible pools and compute exact sampling expectations, removing candidate Monte Carlo error. Use hypergeometric HR only with a verified compatible tie policy. Exact expectations and realized draws remain distinct.

Save local seed-42 streams, candidates and denominators; insufficient pools remain unavailable. Preserve one GRU4Rec checkpoint per category. These are conditional training-prefix measurements, vulnerable to memorization and selection effects. Only unchanged host macro validation HR@10 selects subsequent training changes.

idea.description: Extend the existing GRU4Rec diagnostic with a paired uniform-versus-frequency-matched candidate panel. Freeze each training-prefix history, target, checkpoint and scorer; change only the distribution drawing 99 unique training-unseen distractors. Use fresh independent draws for sampling estimates, retain previous frozen sets separately, and optionally compute exact finite-pool expectations through chunked scoring.
idea.motivation: Reported execution checks pass, but exported-predictor parity, temporal-effect values and official validation results remain unavailable. Electronics exhibits weaker sampled training separation for low-frequency positives. This motivates candidate-distribution sensitivity analysis before attributing the pattern to popularity bias, recurrent forgetting or user intent. Frequency matching may make separation easier or harder; it neither corrects the host metric nor identifies the cause of validation errors. At 10% progress, a bounded diagnostic remains feasible, although a controlled training-sampler experiment is the stronger next step if the immediate objective becomes predictive improvement.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve existing probes, ModelView compatibility and the separate twenty-user full-catalog unseen-item recommendation workflow, with five real training users per category. Access the actual module through view.model and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. No unavailable ratings, reviews, item categories, prices, stores or simulator traits are needed.

Prespecify the panel before inspecting its results. Reuse the existing explicitly user-indexed cases only if their documented construction matches this protocol; otherwise construct cases from public training histories and report the difference rather than silently pooling protocols. Sort unique serialized user IDs lexicographically, reject serialization collisions, select the first at most 200 eligible users per category, take each final training interaction as target, and retain its preceding history truncated to the baseline external width. Require at least five retained nonpadding interactions. Record raw and retained lengths, target index, truncation, stable user index, exclusion counts and category. Targets can have participated in fitting. Never recover user identities from anonymous loader rows or read hidden evaluation files. Compute item frequencies from all unchanged training-split interaction occurrences, including repeats; retain bands 1–4, 5–19 and 20+. Frequency is not exposure. Items with zero training frequency remain eligible for the uniform pool if they are real catalog items, but are outside these positive-target bands; report their pool count explicitly.

Exclude padding, reserved IDs, the target and the user's complete original training history from negative eligibility. Define U_u as the remaining real-item pool and F_u as its subset in the target's frequency band. Require both pools to contain at least 99 items. Do not broaden bands, change exclusions or sample with replacement to rescue cases. Report exclusions and pool sizes by dataset and target band. Compare both conditions on this same complete-case subset. Preserve separately labeled uniform-only results for otherwise eligible cases excluded from the comparison; they have a different user population. Retaining legitimate earlier target occurrences in the input does not relax negative exclusions.

For each complete case, draw five fresh independent sets per condition, each containing 99 unique negatives sampled uniformly without replacement from its pool. Sets can overlap across draws and conditions. Do not insert a reused frozen set into these five replicates: score and report any earlier frozen uniform set separately as one realized-set result. Repeated deterministic scoring supplies no sampling replication. Use np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence([42, category_index, stable_user_index, condition_id, draw_index])) with the fixed category order Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl; condition IDs 300 and 301 identify uniform and matched sampling. Use separate namespace 400 for bootstrap. Persist protocol version, generator/library versions, ordered candidate IDs and seeds. Keep the target first in stored candidate arrays without treating its position as a favorable tie break. Do not consume global training RNG streams.

Score each unchanged history once and reuse its final feature across candidate sets. Respect the existing NumPy/Tensor ModelView adapter and gather the maximum nonzero input position, never count minus one. Use predict_score so all learned projections, nonlinearities and biases remain included. Verify finite features, finite scores and expected candidate dimensions. Run in torch.inference_mode() with evaluation mode, preserving every module's training flag and Python, NumPy, Torch and CUDA RNG states and restoring them in finally. Require the applicable execution checks; an unavailable exported-predictor check stays explicitly unavailable rather than being counted as a pass.

Primary per-draw statistics are target-minus-maximum-negative margin and strict negative-win fraction, sum(s_negative > s_target)/99. Report exact target-score tie counts separately. Define negative-win damage as matched minus uniform, and margin damage as uniform minus matched, so positive contrasts consistently mean weaker sampled separation under matched candidates. These strict-score statistics do not incorporate evaluator tie breaking. Rank and HR@10 require the pinned diagnostic ranking helper and documented tie policy; otherwise return null with a reason. Diagnostic HR is never official host validation HR@10. Save counts and native score dtype; float64 conversion for summaries cannot recover precision lost during inference.

Average all five prescribed draws within each user and condition, then compute paired user contrasts and equally weighted category means. A nonfinite or failed draw invalidates that user's corresponding complete comparison; report failures without silently averaging fewer draws. For U complete users, estimate each condition's candidate Monte Carlo variance as sum_u s_u,c^2/(5*U^2), using sample variance across its five fresh draws. Independent condition streams give contrast MCSE sqrt(sum_u (s_u,uniform^2+s_u,matched^2)/(5*U^2)). Five draws yield noisy variance estimates; report replication counts and avoid precise coverage claims. Reused sets across subsequently compared models require covariance-aware paired differences, not independent-stream formulas.

Optional exact reference: prespecify at most the first 20 complete users per category and a synchronized diagnostic wall-time cap of 60 seconds per category. Chunk-score their complete U_u pools through the same frozen network and reuse subset scores for F_u; use candidate chunks of at most 4096 and CPU float64 reductions. Report completed users, operations skipped and budget termination. Do not merge exact-subset and Monte Carlo-all-user summaries as though they share a population. This is scoring by the existing network, not an independently fitted popularity or retrieval scorer.

For a pool of N>=99 negatives and n=99, strict negative-win expectation is K_strict/N, where K_strict counts scores strictly greater than the target. Its sampling variance is p*(1-p)*(N-n)/(n*(N-1)). If the pinned tie policy supplies a candidate-subset-invariant total ordering, count K negatives ordered ahead of the target and compute exact expected HR@10 as HypergeomCDF(9; N,K,n), preferably with scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf. Otherwise exact HR remains null unless the actual tie mechanism is explicitly integrated; do not substitute K_strict when tied negatives can outrank the target.

For sorted ascending pool scores a_1,...,a_N, exact expected sampled maximum is sum_{j=n}^N a_j*C(j-1,n-1)/C(N,n). Compute weights with stable log-combinations or a stable normalized recurrence, including tied scores; verify nonnegative weights summing to one within a documented numerical tolerance and expectation bounds between a_n and a_N. Exact expected margin is s_target minus this expectation. N=n is the deterministic entire-pool case. Exact sampling expectations have zero candidate-draw Monte Carlo error conditional on the scored finite pool, although numerical error and user/model uncertainty remain. The variance of an individual random draw is not uncertainty in the exact expectation. Preserve realized frozen-set, fresh-draw and exact-expectation results as separate fields.

For optional intervals, use 2,000 CPU bootstrap replicates, resampling complete user records and retaining all their conditions and realized draws. Require at least 30 complete users for Monte Carlo-panel intervals; the exact reference subset capped at 20 therefore receives descriptive summaries only. Label intervals empirical selected-user reweighting intervals conditional on the fitted checkpoint and realized candidates, without population-coverage claims from deterministic user selection. Do not resample draws within users or add bootstrap uncertainty and MCSE as independent components. Report history-length and repeat-target/novel-target slices with denominators and small-slice warnings. Repeated versus novel refers to occurrence of the target in the retained input; record occurrence in the complete prefix separately.

Category-local macro fields remain null. External aggregation requires all four category outputs and gives categories equal weights. Resample users independently within categories using shared resampled indices across conditions. For independent category sampling streams, macro candidate MCSE is sqrt(sum_c MCSE_c^2)/4. Intervals exclude retraining, seed variation and adaptive search-selection uncertainty. Missing categories or required measurements yield null with reasons.

Update the interpreter using actual metrics and definitions. Distinguish candidate-distribution sensitivity from popularity bias, training fit from generalization, and exact expectations from realized candidate sets. Unobserved negatives can be relevant. Frequency matching changes the question being measured and is not an unbiased evaluation correction. Training-prefix targets can be memorized; good panel results can reflect shortcut learning. Existing temporal probes can describe sequence dependence when their actual values are available, but cannot establish causal intent. Titles/descriptions can support a future textual stress panel, without proving compatibility, mood or irrelevance.

Consider alternatives without combining independently fitted predictors. A subsequent controlled training experiment can compare uniform negatives against q(i) proportional to training_frequency(i)^0.5 on positive-frequency training items, holding negative count, loss and all other settings fixed; document eligible support, exclusions and any rejection distribution. With the sampler fixed, a separate subsequent experiment can compare the existing loss against regularized BPR-max. Specify that loss and regularization coefficient before execution rather than changing loss and sampler together. GRU4Rec evidence motivates these experiments but does not guarantee Amazon gains. Training/validation curves and gradient norms can help distinguish incomplete optimization from memorization. Target-frequency validation slices and score–frequency associations are supplementary only when supplied by an authorized validation interface; do not independently inspect hidden labels or change the evaluator.

This selected proposal changes diagnosis only and requires no retraining or predictor architecture change. Preserve exactly one independently trained GRU4Rec checkpoint per category, all four routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch and single-GPU execution. No additional fitted scorer, ensemble, fusion or checkpoint averaging is introduced. Future architecture changes require synchronized training, checkpoint configuration, ModelView and embedded predictor-writer updates. Record synchronized diagnostic runtime and all adaptive search exposure against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Do not read other trials, hidden test files or external datasets. Only unchanged host macro validation HR@10 selects models. No execution success, causal explanation or recommendation improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved = capture_all_module_modes_and_global_rng_states()
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with inference_mode():
                existing = run_existing_family_specific_probes(train_loader)
                if not required_execution_checks_pass(existing):
                    return merge_unavailable_panel(existing, reason='execution checks failed or unresolved')
                counts = count_all_training_interaction_occurrences(self.view.user_train['History'])
                cases = reuse_protocol_matching_cases_or_build_prespecified_cases(
                    max_users=200, target='final_training_interaction',
                    minimum_prefix_length=5, order='lexicographic_serialized_user_id')
                records, exclusions, exact_records, frozen_records = [], [], [], []
                exact_timer = synchronized_timer()
                for case in cases:
                    uniform_pool = real_catalog_items_excluding_complete_training_history_and_target(case)
                    matched_pool = sorted(i for i in uniform_pool
                        if frequency_band(counts[i]) == frequency_band(counts[case.target]))
                    if min(len(uniform_pool), len(matched_pool)) < 99:
                        exclusions.append(explicit_case_exclusion(case, uniform_pool, matched_pool))
                        preserve_separate_uniform_only_summary_if_available(case)
                        continue
                    features = compatible_log2feats(self.view, case.sequence)
                    final = gather_maximum_nonzero_position(features, case.sequence)
                    record = initialize_case_record_with_protocol_and_pool_sizes(case)
                    for condition_id, pool in [(300, uniform_pool), (301, matched_pool)]:
                        for draw in range(5):
                            rng = default_rng(SeedSequence([
                                42, fixed_category_index, case.stable_index, condition_id, draw]))
                            negatives = rng.choice(sorted(pool), size=99, replace=False)
                            candidates = concatenate([case.target], negatives)
                            scores = compatible_predict_score(self.view, final, candidates)
                            require_finite_scores_and_expected_shape(scores)
                            record.save(condition_id, draw, candidates, scores,
                                margin=scores[0] - max(scores[1:]),
                                negative_win_fraction=mean(scores[1:] > scores[0]),
                                exact_target_ties=sum(scores[1:] == scores[0]),
                                rank_and_hr=pinned_rank_helper_or_null(scores, candidates))
                    records.append(record)
                    if earlier_frozen_uniform_set_available(case):
                        frozen_records.append(score_and_label_separate_realized_set(case, final))
                    if case_is_in_first_20_complete_cases(case) and exact_timer.seconds < 60:
                        pool_scores = chunk_score_same_model(final, uniform_pool, chunk_size=4096)
                        for pool in [uniform_pool, matched_pool]:
                            scores = select_pool_scores(pool_scores, pool)
                            N, n = len(pool), 99
                            p = count(scores > target_score) / N
                            expected_max = stable_finite_population_expected_max(scores, n)
                            exact_hr = None
                            if pinned_tie_policy_has_subset_invariant_total_order():
                                K = count_negatives_preceding_target_under_pinned_order(scores, pool)
                                exact_hr = scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf(9, N, K, n)
                            exact_records.append({
                                'expected_strict_negative_win_fraction': p,
                                'single_draw_variance': p*(1-p)*(N-n)/(n*(N-1)),
                                'expected_margin': target_score - expected_max,
                                'expected_hr10': exact_hr,
                                'candidate_mcse': 0,
                                'population': 'prespecified completed exact-reference cases'})
                summary = average_five_draws_within_user_then_pair_conditions(records)
                summary.mcse = independent_fresh_draw_mcse(records, draws=5)
                summary.intervals = paired_complete_user_reweighting_bootstrap_or_null(
                    records, replicates=2000, minimum_users=30, seed_namespace=400)
                summary.slices = frequency_length_and_repeat_target_slices_with_denominators(records)
                summary.frozen_sets = separately_summarize(frozen_records)
                summary.exact_reference = separately_summarize(exact_records)
                summary.exclusions = exclusions
                summary.macro = None  # Requires external aggregation of all four categories.
                save_trial_local_protocol_candidates_scores_counts_and_runtime()
                return merge_metrics_and_explicit_definitions(existing, summary)
        finally:
            restore_all_module_modes_and_global_rng_states(saved)

def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return prompt_containing_measured_metrics_and_definitions(
        raw_diagnosis,
        limits=['conditional training-prefix candidate sensitivity',
                'frequency matching is not unbiased evaluation or proof of popularity bias',
                'frequency is not exposure; unobserved candidates may be relevant',
                'training targets may be memorized',
                'frozen realized sets, fresh draws and exact expectations are distinct',
                'missing measurements are not zero effects',
                'no causal intent or official validation improvement inference'])

originality.positive: The specific pairing of target-frequency-matched pools, preserved history/model controls and optional exact finite-pool expectations creates a reproducible diagnostic adaptation.
originality.negative: Popularity-cohort diagnosis, candidate sampling analysis and finite-population expectations are established. The earlier score of 4 overstated novelty without demonstrated diagnostic value.

future_potential.positive: Can motivate controlled single-model sampling and loss experiments while distinguishing candidate-distribution effects from changes in model parameters.
future_potential.negative: It neither identifies the cause of low validation HR@10 nor directly improves recommendations. Training-prefix results may transfer poorly to held-out targets, limiting the earlier rating of 7.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses one trained checkpoint per category and existing scoring interfaces; the basic panel needs no GRU instrumentation or retraining.
code_difficulty.negative: The earlier score of 3 understated complete-case accounting, independent replication, exact tie compatibility, stable finite-pool calculations, runtime controls and uncertainty reporting.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation — Walid Krichene and Steffen Rendle, KDD 2020
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation.
Explains why small candidate samples can measure behavior closer to AUC than the intended full-catalog ranking metric.
Supports separating conditional candidate diagnostics from the unchanged pinned selection benchmark.
limitations: Does not establish that frequency matching recovers full-catalog HR@10 or improves this GRU4Rec model.
Does not justify modifying the host evaluator.

related_work.title: Evaluating Performance and Bias of Negative Sampling in Large-Scale Sequential Recommendation Models — Arushi Prakash, Dimitrios Bermperidis and Srivas Chennu, 2024
contributions: Compares six training negative-sampling strategies using SASRec on MovieLens-10M, Amazon Beauty and RetailRocket, averaging 20 runs according to the supplied search results.
Uses full-catalog evaluation and target training-frequency strata to expose disparities concealed by aggregate accuracy.
Reports dataset-dependent tradeoffs between popularity balance and aggregate accuracy.
limitations: Studies training samplers rather than validating target-frequency-matched evaluation negatives.
Uses a different backbone and datasets; its mechanisms cannot be assumed for the four Amazon GRU4Rec models.
Training frequency does not measure exposure or preference; reported RetailRocket variance warrants caution.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations — Balázs Hidasi and Alexandros Karatzoglou, 2018
contributions: Provides direct GRU4Rec evidence that negative sampling and loss design interact.
Explains gradient dilution when conventional pairwise objectives average over many easy negatives and develops ranking-max objectives.
Motivates changing sampler and loss in separate controlled experiments while fixing negative count.
limitations: Its session-based Recall/MRR@20 results do not guarantee gains on this Amazon HR@10 task.
Simply increasing negative count or adopting popularity sampling is not uniformly beneficial.
A reproducible BPR-max trial still requires an explicit regularizer and prespecified coefficient.

related_work.title: Candidate Set Sampling
contributions: The supplied search results emphasize interactions among candidate sampling, popularity and missing observations.
Supports distinguishing candidate-distribution sensitivity from a claim of popularity bias.
limitations: Does not make frequency-matched candidates an unbiased evaluation design.
Does not identify the cause of this model's validation errors.

related_work.title: Hypergeometric Distribution
contributions: Provides the finite-population sampling-without-replacement distribution for outranking counts.
Supports exact expected sampled HR@10 and negative-win moments when eligibility and tie ordering are correctly specified.
limitations: The HR formula requires a compatible fixed ordering relative to the target; score ties cannot be ignored.
Exact candidate-sampling expectations remain conditional on the fitted model, histories and finite pools.

related_work.title: Finite-population order statistics reference supplied in the search results
contributions: Supports combinatorial order-statistic calculations for uniform sampling without replacement.
Motivates computing the expected sampled maximum directly from complete eligible-pool scores.
limitations: Exact calculations require complete pool scoring and numerically stable probability weights.
Removing candidate Monte Carlo error does not remove training uncertainty, selection effects or diagnostic distribution mismatch.

related_work.title: PURE (2026)
contributions: The supplied search summary distinguishes factual correctness from personalized preference alignment.
Supports treating textual association and observed history as limited evidence rather than direct labels of current intent.
limitations: Does not validate frequency-matched candidate sampling.
Unavailable review-derived evidence cannot be imported into this task.
